question: do i need an appointment to talk to a peer advisor at piper? when are they there
expected_answer: No appointment is needed; you can drop in to see a Peer Advisor. The most current Piper pages give Peer Advisor drop-in hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, while an older appointments page lists 8-5pm daily plus 7-9pm on Tuesdays and Wednesdays; an answer that gives the 8:30-5 hours or flags the difference is correct. Peer Advisors help with resumes, cover letters, internships, job searches, Handshake and events.

question: how do I set up a meeting with a career coach and how far ahead do I have to book
expected_answer: Schedule with a career coach through Handshake (Appointments, then pick the category, type, coach, time and in-person or virtual), and request it at least 24 hours before the appointment time. For urgent needs email the coach, call the Piper Center or stop by; coaches also take short drop-ins 3-5 p.m. Monday to Friday (an older page also lists 7-9 p.m. Tuesday and Wednesday).

question: who at piper should I talk to if I'm thinking about law school
expected_answer: Leslie Moore is the Piper Center's pre-law coach (Associate Director, Career Development and Coaching, Pre-Law, Graduate and Professional School) and the catalog's campus contact for law (Tomson Hall 270, 507-786-3143, moore8@stolaf.edu); appointments are scheduled via Handshake.

question: my summer internship is unpaid, how much can the piper center grant actually give me
expected_answer: The current summer funding page says the Piper Center Internship Grant Award provides up to $2,500 toward eligible expenses, students may get less depending on demand (minimal-expense or virtual internships usually get at least $800), and each student can receive it only once. A summer internship generally needs at least 8 weeks and 240 hours. An older FAQ page says the maximum is $2,000 with 60-85% of requests funded; an answer citing $2,500 or flagging the discrepancy is correct.

question: how many hours do I need to work to get 1 full credit for an internship
expected_answer: For 1.0 credit the internship plus academic work must total at least 160 hours, with at least 120 hours devoted to the internship itself (40 for academic work). For comparison, 0.5 credit needs 100 hours (80 on site) and 0.25 credit needs 65 hours (55 on site).

question: whats the deadline to register an academic internship for jterm
expected_answer: The deadline to register an academic internship for J-Term is December 15 (Fall is September 23, Spring is February 23). Registering soon after a deadline may be possible but can take longer and the Registrar may charge a Late Add Fee.

question: can first years go to the minnesota private colleges job and internship fair? and is there a bus
expected_answer: No, the fair is open only to sophomores, juniors and seniors, and advance registration in Handshake is required. A bus departs at 8:15am from the Buntrock Commons Turnaround (lower entrance) and returns at 11:30 or 1:00pm from outside the Convention Center.

question: when is the government and nonprofit career fair this year
expected_answer: The 2026 Government & Nonprofit Career Fair is Friday, October 23, 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM in the Great Hall of Coffman Memorial Union at the University of Minnesota. Registration on Handshake was due Friday, October 16 at 11:59 PM; it is free and the Piper Center provides transportation. As of October 28, 2026 the fair has already taken place, which a good answer may note.

question: who do i contact about applying for a fulbright
expected_answer: The pages conflict. The Nationally Competitive Fellowships pages name Professor Douglas Casson (casson@stolaf.edu), Co-Director of External Fellowships and Scholarships, as the Fulbright campus contact and say to meet with him (ideally in the spring of junior year) before the campus deadline. An older Piper Center page says to contact Heather Campbell for Fulbright and Kathryn Ananda-Owens for other fellowships. Casson is the preferred answer; Campbell is acceptable only if the conflict is flagged.

question: studying for the GRE, does piper have prep books I can borrow?
expected_answer: Yes, the Piper Center lends out GRE, GMAT and LSAT practice books; stop by to check them out. The page also points to free practice exams through Learning Express with a Northfield Public Library card (available with your student ID).

question: is CSCI 121 ok if ive never coded before? what language is it in
expected_answer: Yes, CSCI 121 Introduction to Computer Science expects no prior programming experience. It uses Python and is offered each semester.

question: what do I have to take before psych 230
expected_answer: PSYCH 230 Research Methods in Psychology requires PSYCH 125 plus one intro statistics course: STAT 110, SDS 172, or ECON 260.

question: does econ 121 count toward the econ major
expected_answer: No, ECON 121 Principles of Economics does not count toward the economics major, but it is the prerequisite for all higher-level economics courses (the department says the intro course is not required but is the prerequisite for the core courses and Level II electives). The catalog says it is offered each semester; the department page says fall, interim and spring.

question: what classes are required for the computer science major
expected_answer: The CS major is set up by an individual plan/contract (CSMaP) with a CS faculty member, 11 courses: CSCI 121 (or 125, PHYS 130 or approved prior experience), CSCI 221, 241, 251, 263 and 353, plus MATH 220 and MATH 234, plus three upper-level electives. At least two electives come from the designated list (Operating Systems, Programming Languages, Intro to Machine Learning, Theory of Computation, Foundations of AI in the catalog), and at least one elective must be level 300.

question: how many classes is the psych major
expected_answer: The psychology major is 10 courses: 9 in psychology plus 1 statistics course. It includes PSYCH 125 and PSYCH 230, one course from each of three different core areas, two level III courses, two psychology electives, and an intro statistics course; at least six PSYCH courses must be taken through St. Olaf.

question: what chem do bio majors need to take
expected_answer: Biology majors take eight biology courses plus a year of chemistry: either CHEM 122 and CHEM 126, or CHEM 125 and CHEM 126. CHEM 126 requires completion of a calculus course (MATH 120 is a pre or co-requisite).

question: poli sci major requirements?
expected_answer: Political science majors take at least nine courses, with no more than three at level I, PSCI 220 Analyzing Politics and Policies, and at least two level III seminars. They must take at least one course in each of four subfields: American politics and public policy, comparative politics, international relations, and political theory.

question: when do you apply for the nursing major and whats the gpa cutoff
expected_answer: You can be considered for direct admission when applying to St. Olaf from high school, or apply through regular admission in the fall semester of your sophomore year; the major begins spring of sophomore year. Applicants need a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (prerequisites taken for a letter grade with at least a C), and admission is limited and competitive.

question: how many credits do i need to graduate and how many have to be upper level
expected_answer: You need 35 St. Olaf credits to graduate, and 18 of them must be at level II or III (courses numbered 200 and above).

question: how many classes can i take S/U and do they count for gen eds
expected_answer: Students may take up to 6 credits S/U as long as the 24-graded-credit requirement is met. An S means C- or higher. Only .25-credit courses taken S/U can fulfill OLE Core requirements (1.00 or .50 credit S/U courses do not), and at most one 1.00-credit S/U course can count toward a major.

question: i missed the drop deadline, can i still drop a class?
expected_answer: Yes, by petition: a late drop (withdrawal) uses the Petition form on the registrar's website, signed by the instructor, your advisor and you, and must be submitted by the last day of classes of that term. The course stays on your record with a W; an unreported drop results in an F.

question: if i take a class at a community college over the summer will it transfer back
expected_answer: After matriculating, a student may transfer a maximum of 4.00 St. Olaf credits, and only two OLE Core attributes can come from them. The course must be graded C or higher (P/S grades are not accepted) and an official transcript is required; get the course pre-approved by the Registrar using the Transfer Credit Approval Form for Current Students.

question: how much AP credit can I bring in as a first year
expected_answer: New first-year students can receive at most 6.00 St. Olaf credits from all pre-college work (AP, IB, Cambridge A Level, PSEO/CIS). Exam credit is awarded first up to 6.00, PSEO up to 4.00, and at most six OLE Core attributes can be fulfilled through pre-college credit.

question: what gets you put on academic notice
expected_answer: You go on academic notice if you do not meet Satisfactory Academic Progress (completing 67% of attempted courses and a cumulative GPA of 1.80, 1.90 or 2.00 depending on credits earned), or if you earn two or more grades of D+, D, D-, F or U in 1.0-credit fall or spring courses. Students on notice must meet with their Success Coach to make an academic success plan.

question: do I have to do a j term every single year
expected_answer: Not every year: you need three January term courses completed in three separate January terms (transfer students with at least sophomore standing need two), and one must be taken in the first year since first-year students must register for a J-Term course. You can take only one course during a January term.

question: what gpa do you need for summa cum laude
expected_answer: Summa cum laude requires a cumulative GPA of 3.90 (magna cum laude 3.75, cum laude 3.60). The GPA is never rounded and honors are conferred at commencement.

question: can one class count for two ole core requirements
expected_answer: Only if at least one of the two requirements is Writing Across the Curriculum, Power and Race, Ethical Reasoning in Context, or the OLE Experience in Practice; otherwise a single course fulfills at most one requirement. First-Year Seminar and Writing and Rhetoric courses cannot double count.

question: I'm on the soccer team, does that count for active body
expected_answer: Yes, varsity athletes can use a season of participation as 0.25 kinesiology credit, which satisfies the Active Body requirement. Only one 0.25 intercollegiate athletics credit can count toward the 35 credits needed to graduate.

question: how many language classes do I need
expected_answer: The World Languages and Cultures requirement is 0-3 courses depending on placement, proficiency or transfer work; most incoming students take at least one and at most three courses at St. Olaf.

question: how do i get writing in the major done
expected_answer: Writing in the Major is fulfilled within your major, through one course or a set of modules across two or more courses, with at least half at the 300 level. Many majors state that completing the major satisfies it.

question: does the OLE experience in practice thing have to be an actual class
expected_answer: No, the OLE Experience in Practice can be satisfied by a non-credit-bearing experience. It involves work that integrates academic and experiential learning, applying classroom ideas in a practical setting.

question: when is the early decision deadline for st olaf
expected_answer: Early Decision I and Early Action applications are due November 1, and Early Decision II and Regular Decision are due January 15. Admission notification is early December for ED I, late December for EA, early February for ED II and late February (catalog: about March 15) for Regular Decision.

question: how much does it cost to go to st olaf for 2026-27
expected_answer: The 2026-2027 comprehensive fee is $81,200: $65,700 tuition, $7,150 housing, $7,850 meal plan and a $500 activities fee (the admissions page lists housing and meals together as $15,000). Taking more than 4.50 credits in a semester costs $1,030 per 0.25 credit over 4.50.

question: what forms do I fill out for financial aid
expected_answer: To be considered for need-based St. Olaf aid you complete both the CSS Profile (code 6638) and the FAFSA (code 002382); the FAFSA alone covers federal and state aid, and merit scholarships need no aid forms. Returning students only redo the FAFSA each year (no CSS Profile after the first year), with an April 30 priority deadline.

question: what classes should I take if I'm pre med
expected_answer: Recommended: MATH 119 or 120; three semesters of biology (typically BIO 150, 227, 233); a general chemistry sequence; CHEM 247 and 248 (organic); CHEM 379 (biochemistry); PHYS 124 and 125; a physiology course (BIO 243 or BIO 247); PSYCH 125; a sociology course; and a statistics course (typically SDS 172). Professor Kevin Crisp, Chair of the Health Professions Committee, advises pre-health students.

question: does my financial aid work if I study abroad
expected_answer: Yes. Students on St. Olaf study abroad/away programs keep the financial aid they would get on campus (federal, state and institutional), except student work. They pay St. Olaf tuition plus program fees and out-of-pocket costs, and all applicants are automatically considered for need-based Smith Center scholarships; the Global Semester costs the same as a semester on campus.

question: what about the concentration?
expected_answer: The neuroscience concentration (for students graduating up to 2029; the new major applies from grad year 2030) is 6 credits: PSYCH 238 Biopsychology and NEURO 239 Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience, two lab electives (the first from Category A), one more elective from Category A, B or C, and one level III seminar. Students must consult the concentration director and develop a contract by the end of sophomore year.

history.content: what do you need for the neuroscience major
The neuroscience major is 8.25 credits: NEURO 125, 210, 251 and 252, NEURO 300 (0.25), NEURO 391, and three approved electives.

question: ok what about if im doing a bachelor of music instead
expected_answer: B.M. students do not need the OLE Experience in Practice, take one of Religion, Faith and Values or Christian Theology in Dialogue (not both), and one of Natural Science or Quantitative and Computational Reasoning. The other requirements (First-Year Seminar, Writing and Rhetoric, Power and Race, Global Histories and Societies, Social Science, Writing Across the Curriculum, Ethical Reasoning, Active Body, Writing in the Major, World Languages) still apply, and vocal performance majors need 112-level courses in two languages, one French or German.

history.content: what gen eds do I need for a BA

For a B.A. you complete the OLE Core: First-Year Seminar, Writing and Rhetoric, Religion Faith and Values, Christian Theology in Dialogue, Power and Race, Global Histories and Societies, Natural Science, Social Science, Writing Across the Curriculum, Quantitative and Computational Reasoning, World Languages, Creativity, OLE Experience in Practice, Ethical Reasoning, Active Body, and Writing in the Major.

question: what if it's over jterm, can i just do the quarter credit version?
expected_answer: No, 0.25-credit academic internships are not an option during J-Term (Interim). St. Olaf's pages disagree about 0.5-credit J-Term internships: some Piper pages say 0.25 and 0.5-credit internships cannot be completed during Interim, while others describe a 0.5-credit J-Term option that doesn't count toward the three-J-Term requirement. A correct answer says 0.25 is not allowed and either flags this conflict or points to the Piper Center to confirm. For 1.0 credit, students usually register for ID 295 or KINES 295.

history.content: how many hours do internships need for credit
For 1.0 credit you need 160 total hours (at least 120 at the internship), for 0.5 credit 100 hours (80 on site), and for 0.25 credit 65 hours (55 on site).

question: what time does stav hall close tonight
expected_answer: Stav Hall dinner runs 4:30-8 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 4:30-7:30 p.m. Friday through Sunday, so on a weeknight like today (Wednesday) it closes at 8 p.m. (Breakfast is 7-9:45 a.m. and lunch 10:30 a.m.-2 p.m. on weekdays.)

question: how much is a student parking permit
expected_answer: For 2026-27 a general student permit (or off-campus living permit) is $300 for the full academic year or $175 per semester (J-Term included), motorcycle/scooter add-ons are $90 and summer is $40, bought through Flex Port. An earlier announcement listed $185 per semester; the current community parking page says $175. First-years need a home address at least 250 miles away to be eligible.

question: what are professor jay demas's office hours this week
expected_answer: The department faculty listings give James (Jay) Demas, Associate Professor of Biology and Physics, office hours of Monday 4:30-5:30, Wednesday 12:00-1:00, Thursday 9:00-10:00 and 4:00-5:00, and Friday 9:00-10:00, plus an appointment calendar. The pages do not confirm this specific week, so a good answer gives these hours and suggests checking with him or his calendar.

question: how do i connect my laptop to the campus wifi
expected_answer: The campus network is St. Olaf eduroam; new students should first remove any other eduroam profiles from their devices, then follow the IT knowledge base article 'Connecting to the Wireless Network (WiFi)' at help.stolaf.edu. For help, the IT Helpdesk is in Rolvaag Library room 353 or at 507-786-3830.

question: is rolvaag library open 24 hours during finals week
expected_answer: The posted hours do not show Rolvaag being open 24 hours, and no special finals-week schedule is posted. Regular hours are about 7:45 a.m. to midnight Monday through Thursday, Saturday 9 a.m.-9 p.m. and Sunday noon to midnight; Friday closing is 9 p.m. in the Fall 2026 update but 7 p.m. on the building hours page. A good answer says 24-hour access is not indicated and suggests checking the posted hours.

question: are there any halloween events on campus this weekend
expected_answer: Yes: PipeScreams, the Halloween organ recital by St. Olaf organ students, is Friday, October 30 at 8:15 p.m. in Boe Memorial Chapel (also livestreamed). On Saturday, October 31 the St. Olaf Festival of Bands concert is at 5 p.m. in Skoglund Auditorium, with band students dressing up for Halloween during the day.

question: when do christmas festival tickets go on sale for students
expected_answer: For 2026, ticket presale runs October 26-30 and the public sale begins November 2; the Orchestra Hall box office handles all ticketing (612-371-5656, tickets@mnorch.org). Performances are at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis on Friday, December 4 at 8 p.m. and Saturday, December 5 at 2 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. No separate student sale is described.

question: if i win an outside scholarship does st olaf just take away my aid
expected_answer: Outside scholarships are added to your St. Olaf award, but if you have need-based aid St. Olaf may have to adjust it: reductions come first from federal student loans, then student employment. Your St. Olaf Grant is reduced only in the rare case that outside scholarships exceed your loans and work and your costs are fully covered. Students should tell the Financial Aid Office the scholarship's name and amount.

question: my dad lost his job this summer, can we ask for more aid?
expected_answer: Yes, through a financial aid appeal: job loss or a significant reduction in income can qualify as a special circumstance. Complete the Special Circumstance Request Form for the right aid year and upload documentation through the secure portal; the job loss must have happened at least six weeks ago with full documentation, and appeals usually take five to ten business days.

question: whats st olafs fafsa school code and when can i start filling it out
expected_answer: St. Olaf's FAFSA code is 002382 (CSS Profile code 6638). The FAFSA for 2027-28 can be completed any time after October 1, 2026 and uses 2025 tax information; there is no fee for the FAFSA.

question: how much can i borrow in federal loans as a sophomore
expected_answer: A dependent sophomore can borrow up to $6,500 in Federal Direct Loans: up to $4,500 subsidized (based on need) plus $2,000 unsubsidized, limited to cost of attendance minus other aid. For 2026-27 the subsidized rate is fixed at 6.52% and there is a 1.057% origination fee.

question: which dorms do first years live in
expected_answer: All first-year students live in the First Year Neighborhood: Ellingson, Kildahl, Thorson and Mohn Halls. Mohn is a ten-story hall that houses first-years and upperclass students by floor.

question: can i live off campus next year? an apartment would be cheaper
expected_answer: Only with an approved Residential Housing Exemption. The approved exemptions are: 23 or older by December 31; living with parents or guardians within 45 driving miles of campus; having completed all major requirements before fall; being married; or being a custodial parent. Financial reasons are not considered, though you can submit extenuating circumstances.

question: how much more does a single cost than a double
expected_answer: Current room rates are $7,150 a year ($3,575 per semester) for multiple occupancy, $8,850 a year ($4,425 per semester) for a single and $10,650 a year ($5,325 per semester) for a premium single, so a single is $1,700 more per year than a double.

question: can i keep a pet in my dorm room
expected_answer: No, pets are not allowed in the residence halls except fish; service animals and emotional support animals are allowed through the Disability and Access Office. The pages conflict on tank size: the Residential Health and Safety page says one tank under 10 gallons per room, while the Residence Life FAQ and The Book say up to 15 gallons; a correct answer gives one and flags the difference or says to confirm.

question: how do i get an official transcript sent somewhere
expected_answer: Order it online through the National Student Clearinghouse (in SIS: Student, Personal, Clearinghouse Services), or in person at Tomson Hall 149 or by mail with the Official Transcript Request Form. Electronic and mailed transcripts cost $8, rush adds $5, and regular electronic processing takes 2-3 business days.

question: im a senior, how do i apply to graduate
expected_answer: Submit the Graduation and Commencement Application in SIS early in the spring semester of the year you will finish (the Registrar emails you when it is added). It asks how your name should appear on the diploma and program, whether you will attend commencement, and how to pronounce your name; also review your degree audit and clear any Student Accounts holds.

question: when do juniors register for spring classes
expected_answer: Spring 2026-27 registration runs by class year from Tuesday, November 3 to Friday, November 6: seniors Tuesday, juniors Wednesday (November 4), sophomores Thursday and first-years Friday. All holds must be removed first; January term registration begins Monday, November 2.

question: ok what if i just want to switch it to S/U instead
expected_answer: The S/U change deadline is the same as the drop deadline: Wednesday, November 11 for a fall semester-length course (Tuesday, November 17 for second-half-of-semester courses). You can take up to 6 credits S/U, S means C- or higher, and only .25-credit S/U courses count toward OLE Core.

history.content: whats the last day to drop a class this semester
For a semester-length fall 2026 course, the last day to drop (with instructor permission) is Wednesday, November 11.

question: do i have to send my SAT or ACT to apply
expected_answer: No, St. Olaf is test-optional: ACT or SAT scores are not required, and applicants without scores are still considered for all merit scholarships. If you do submit, self-reported scores are accepted and St. Olaf superscores; English proficiency tests are required for some international students.

question: what do you get for applying early decision
expected_answer: Students admitted through Early Decision (I or II) get at least a $30,000 St. Olaf scholarship and placement in one of their top two first-year residence halls. The third benefit differs by page: the Apply page says 100% of extra costs for a semester or year study abroad/away program are covered, while the Early Decision page says preferential registration for first-semester classes; a correct answer flags the difference.

question: im at a community college rn, when is the deadline to transfer for fall
expected_answer: The fall transfer deadline is April 1, with admission notification in mid-April (mid-year transfer is November 1). Early Decision and Early Action deadlines apply only to first-year applicants.

question: how do i get a counseling appointment and is it free
expected_answer: Counseling Center services are free for currently enrolled students. To schedule, log in to the Ole Care Student Portal and message the Counseling Center Front Desk with your availability; crisis appointments are available by calling. For an emergency call 911, Public Safety at 507-786-3666, or South Central Crisis Support at 877-399-3040.

question: is health services open on saturday? pretty sure i have strep
expected_answer: No, Health Services is closed on weekends. Appointments are Monday-Friday 8:30 a.m.-4:00 p.m. (closed noon-1), booked by calling 507-786-3063 or through the OleCare portal; it is in New Hall (east entrance). Visits are free but some tests and over-the-counter items cost money, and in an emergency call 911 or Public Safety at 507-786-3666.

question: can i book a study room in the library
expected_answer: Yes, select rooms in Rolvaag and Halvorson Music Library can be reserved for up to 4 hours per day, at least 24 hours in advance. The Fall 2026 update says to book at go.stolaf.edu/spaces under 'Library Spaces', while the Reserve a Space page mentions the WebCheckout system; reservable rooms have signs beside them.

question: how do i start a new club
expected_answer: Gather at least ten interested members, find a faculty or staff advisor, draft a constitution (examples on the SGA website), complete the online organization recognition form, and connect with the SGA Involvement Board for next steps.

question: when can i apply to study abroad for fall 2027
expected_answer: Semester and year program applications open November 10, 2026 in the Smith Center's online system; deadlines depend on the program, either December 1, 2026 or February 16, 2027. Most semester and year programs also require a secondary application after acceptance.

question: how much does it pay and when do i apply
expected_answer: CURI summer researchers earn $14.50/hour for up to 40 hours a week for up to 10 weeks (late May to early August), with on-campus housing support. Applications are due in February (February 16 for summer 2026) via the online form, and offers go out in mid-March.

history.content: CURI's summer program offers paid, faculty-mentored research and inquiry positions in all disciplines, mostly about ten weeks on campus from late May to early August.

question: i placed into spanish 112 but im nervous, can i just take 111
expected_answer: Probably not: Spanish 111 is for true beginners, so the department avoids placing students with prior experience there and asks you to register for the level you placed into. Your instructor double-checks placement in the first days of class, you can share concerns with them at the start of the semester (not before), and the first weeks of 112 review 111 material, with supplemental instruction or tutoring available.
